guideline: Participants decided which summary was better based on criteria: Succinctness (avoid repetition), Informativeness (capture important information), Fluency (fluent and grammatical). For WikiCatSum, outputs were compared based on information in the gold summary.
Crowdworkers compare two summaries and select the better one for each of the listed criteria.

Human participants were presented with the output of two systems (and the original document) and asked to decide which one was better according to the following criteria: Succinctness (Does the summary avoid repetition?), Informativeness (Does the summary capture the document's most important information?), and Fluency (Is the summary fluent and grammatical?).

changes_made.explanation: The extracted human evaluation metadata is accurate and complete

overall_notes: The paper focuses on abstractive text summarization using self-knowledge distillation with noise injection. The extraction quality is good - all yes/no answers are correct, and the metadata is mostly accurate. Minor normalization was applied to model names and metrics. The paper conducts comprehensive evaluation using both automatic metrics (ROUGE, FactCC) and human evaluation with clear criteria.
